source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
Corn smut (ជម្ងឺផ្សិតខ្សៅ, Ustilago): this fungal disease is observed on corn, with symptoms appearing on the leaves as brownish marks with a yellowish tinge. It develops at temperatures of about 20-30 degrees Celsius with high humidity. It spreads on the above-ground parts of the plant, especially tissue that is actively growing vigorously. This disease is caused by the fungus Kabatiella zeae (as recorded in the source), which produces galls/swellings on the leaves, stem, tassel, and ear. In the early stage the galls appear whitish or watery-silver in color, later turning brownish, especially forming on ear husks and kernels. The galls contain a black, sooty spore mass inside once mature; they can rupture and release black powdery spores that spread to infect other plants.

Prevention and control measures include disease scouting/observation, timely and appropriate planting practices, using clean, disease-tested seed, and removing/destroying infected plant debris before it can produce and spread new spores, particularly ensuring seed lots used for planting are free of the pathogen.
